channel.title: Horizon Brief
channel.description: A clearer view of world affairs, technology, business, science and climate. Concise English briefings, with attributed sources and transparent editorial checks.

item.title: France protests end in clashes as interior ministry reports 565 arrests
item.description: About 320,000 people joined rallies nationwide, down from 410,000 a week earlier. Police say a hardcore of several hundred rioters attacked officers in Paris, where one officer was hit by a Molotov cocktail.

item.title: Binance says it has replaced 90% of $6.3bn hack losses as FBI blames North Korea
item.description: The exchange says users will not bear the cost of the record theft, drawing on its Secure Asset Fund, a futures insurance pool and corporate treasury. The FBI attributed the attack to a North Korea-affiliated group it calls TraderTraitor.

item.title: Data centers become a midterm flashpoint — even in Brooklyn
item.description: A TechCrunch account of a New York election event finds AI and data-center backlash surfacing far from the server farms, as a report counts nearly $200 billion in projects delayed, stalled or blocked in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Best Buy adds a $100 gift card to touchscreen MacBook Pro preorders
item.description: The retailer is pairing a gift card with preorders of Apple's touch-enabled MacBook Pro, while macOS adds small interface changes for finger input.

item.title: Police Arrest Protesters at First Mass Rally Against Palestine Action Ban Under Burnham
item.description: More than 100 people demonstrated outside the US embassy in London against the proscription of Palestine Action, with arrests beginning as organisers accused the Met of fearing 'US embarrassment'.

item.title: MoD Documents: UK Police Erred in Ceding Airbase Assault Case to US Military
item.description: Internal ministry documents say Cambridgeshire police should not have handed the investigation of a US fighter pilot to American military authorities, as a cross-government inquiry examines how serious crimes involving US personnel end up outside British courts.

item.title: Political text messages are hard to stop, and the fixes are mostly future-facing
item.description: The Verge reports there is no overnight fix for unwanted political texts, though readers can reduce future exposure. The available excerpt does not detail the mechanisms or figures.

item.title: Molly, a Signal fork, has gone three months without an update, leaving known fixes unpatched
item.description: A community post says the fork's last release was v8.19.2-4 on 31 July and recommends switching to mainline Signal until Molly resumes regular updates.

item.title: AI writing detectors flagged a 20-year professional. She lost the book proposal.
item.description: NPR reports that detection tools can disagree sharply on the same text, and that writers are now changing how they write to avoid being accused.

item.title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
item.description: Ars Technica reports that long-distance seabird flights home may disrupt the birds' internal clocks, a finding with implications for how researchers interpret migration timing.

item.title: Healey threatens veto on offshore wind projects that do not cut bills
item.description: The chancellor says ministers will only sign off new subsidy contracts if the grid can absorb the power without raising consumer costs, as a £3bn energy budget cut sharpens questions about Labour's clean power target.

item.title: Starmer: UK must move closer to Europe as US ties shift under Trump
item.description: In his first major political intervention since leaving No 10, Keir Starmer said the change in the US relationship is unlikely to reverse after Trump, and that a stronger Europe needs Britain at its heart.

item.title: Sherrock beats world No 1 Littler on Netflix's live darts show
item.description: Fallon Sherrock defeated Luke Littler on Beat Luke Littler at Manchester Central, a result the streamer had planned contingency programming for in case the world champion fell early.

item.title: TechCrunch reviewer took two iPhones on vacation; the $2K Duo won out
item.description: Sarah Perez carried the foldable iPhone Duo alongside her iPhone 17 Pro Max as a safety net. She used the Duo more, and came home not wanting to switch back.

item.title: FDA Moves to Withdraw Tavneos Approval Over Manipulated Trial Data
item.description: The agency says ChemoCentryx re-adjudicated pivotal trial results after unblinding. Amgen, which bought the company for nearly $4 billion, now argues the drug should stay on the market.

item.title: Justice Department Moves to Set Aside Alaska Ballots in Criminal Probe of Senate Candidate
item.description: Federal prosecutors want certain ballots isolated while they investigate whether voters were confused by a Senate candidate who shares the Republican incumbent's name.

item.title: UK Budget: Energy Bill Help, Pension Rise and the ISA U-Turn Explained
item.description: A £300-plus January energy bill increase looms, VAT on electricity is extended to July, gas standing charges are set to go, and the cash ISA cut is scrapped.

item.title: Obsidian Canvas and Heptabase: How File-First and Card-First Design Shape Spatial Notes
item.description: A comparison of the two tools' data models finds that Obsidian stores visual arrangements in standalone .canvas files, while Heptabase treats whiteboards as views over a central card library.

item.title: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Term as Brazil's President, Defeating Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: With 100% of votes counted, Lula took 51.79% to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.21%, a margin of 4.4 million votes. Bolsonaro refused to concede and said his legal team would seek to annul the result.

item.title: Paulina Borsook's 'Cyberselfish' Returns in New Tin House Edition
item.description: TechCrunch reports that the 2000 book on techno-libertarian culture is coming back into print, with the author reflecting on Silicon Valley's leadership class and AI in a new interview.

item.title: Data centre backlash grows as AI demand reshapes towns and grids
item.description: BBC reporting describes concern over power, water and noise alongside claims of jobs and tax revenue. A separate Apollo economist's assessment adds context on corporate AI returns.

item.title: Loggers Say Roadless Rule Repeal Won't Fix Their Biggest Problems
item.description: NPR reports that Oregon timber operators face fuel costs, labor shortages and a reduced mill base as the administration pursues a proposed Roadless Rule repeal.

item.title: AI Models Are Reshaping Hurricane Forecasting, but Humans Still Decide
item.description: NPR reports that DeepMind's model outperformed rivals on Isaias' track but trailed the official blended forecast on intensity. Human forecasters remain central to interpreting the results.

item.title: Special Education Teachers Describe Joy, Isolation and a Deepening Shortage
item.description: NPR's special education diaries find a field stretched by rising student numbers, heavy paperwork and thin staffing, even as teachers say relationships with students keep them in the work.

item.title: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks on El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
item.description: Remarks at a Port Huron rally drew criticism from a former Arab American outreach ally, while El-Sayed rejected loyalty allegations in the Senate contest against Mike Rogers.

item.title: Talarico Takes Aim at Musk in Texas Senate Bid: 'Texas Is Not for Sale'
item.description: The Democratic Senate candidate rallied at his alma mater, framing his race against Attorney General Ken Paxton around small-dollar fundraising and a single billionaire backer.

item.title: UK regulators propose easing City accountability rules
item.description: Bank of England and FCA plans would cut reporting on lower-level misconduct and free 140,000 managers from extra checks, with regulators estimating about £2bn in savings over a decade.

item.title: Pascal raises $8.5M to develop CO2-cartridge heat pump and refrigeration tech
item.description: The startup says its cartridge design could be about 20% more efficient than existing models, and it has signed a pilot with a multinational beverage company.

item.title: BBC Reports Expected Income Caps for Your First Home Loan Scheme
item.description: The BBC reports that income limits for the government-backed Your First Home equity loan scheme are expected to be confirmed at next week's Budget, with the Conservatives criticizing the plans and developers urging speed.

item.title: Barclays Plans 5,000 Job Cuts as Executives Cite Technology and AI Gains
item.description: The bank links the measures to savings planned for 2027. Unite challenges its approach, calling for workers to gain new skills as technology changes.

item.title: OpenAI Opens Decisions API to All Customers, Challenging TypeSafe's Jev
item.description: The API, announced at OpenAI's September developer day, became available to all customers Thursday. OpenAI says it reconfigured ChatGPT Luna rather than building a dedicated decision model.

item.title: GM Plans OnStar AI Assistant for 2027 Cadillac Lyriq, Details Data Controls
item.description: GM says the assistant will debut in the coming months. Its data-sharing statements include consent controls and possible limits on features when customers decline to share information.

item.title: Survey: Managers Back AI but Find It Harder to Gauge Staff Contribution
item.description: A Nielsen survey commissioned by Monday.com found senior leaders enthusiastic about AI yet spending more time reviewing output, reworking evaluations and bracing to oversee more agents than people.

item.title: Mach9 raises $34M Series A after pivot to AI-assisted CAD software
item.description: The company, founded in 2021 as Mach9 Robotics, says nearly 100 private-beta customers have used its AI CAD tool on more than 2,500 projects. First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners co-led the round.

item.title: Recursive Releases Flint, a Free Laptop Coding Model It Says AI Largely Built
item.description: The startup says its Eureka Machine assisted nearly every stage of Flint's development, yielding a 40 billion parameter model that runs offline and is free to download under an open source license.

item.title: Canva Launches Canva Craft, Its First In-House Image Generation Model
item.description: The design platform says the model, built by its research team with contributions from Leonardo.ai researchers, is available now through the Dream Lab tab, with API access planned.

item.title: Nirva Raises $25M as It Prepares a Voice-Filtering AI Pendant
item.description: The startup, founded by two former Meta Reality Labs employees and a fashion entrepreneur, announced a $25 million pre-Series A round. Its $249 pendant is set to take orders in November.

item.title: Commerce Letters of Intent Cover Up to $389 Million in Energy Semiconductor R&D
item.description: Four companies are named for potential CHIPS Act awards covering fusion power electronics, gallium nitride devices and ultra-high-purity quartz, with Helion's share the largest at up to $175 million.

item.title: Meta Plans New Non-Voting Share Class to Help Fund AI Push
item.description: The company confirmed on its third-quarter earnings call that it intends to distribute a new class of non-voting stock to existing shareholders, with trading expected to begin in 2027.

item.title: Tesla Says It Will Sell Cybercab to Customers by End of Year, TechCrunch Reports
item.description: The announcement comes as federal regulators examine whether the vehicle meets safety standards, according to TechCrunch. Tesla's CEO framed the Cybercab as transport-as-a-service rather than a car for owners.

item.title: Japan's MMX probe heads for Phobos on sample-return voyage
item.description: The $578 million mission is in stable condition after launch, with a rover drop and up to two Phobos landings planned before a 2030 departure from Mars and a 2031 capsule landing in South Australia.

item.title: Rays Take AL Pennant, Set Up First-Title World Series Against Brewers
item.description: Tampa Bay closed out Cleveland in Game 6 of the ALCS and will meet Milwaukee in a Fall Classic where neither club has won a championship. Game 1 is Friday in Milwaukee.

item.title: Report: Anthropic and Nscale in Talks on Another $45B Compute Deal
item.description: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, says the two companies could announce a second $45 billion compute agreement about a month after their first, though talks are ongoing and terms may change.

item.title: European Commission names 13 winners of 2026 New European Bauhaus Prizes
item.description: The laureates come from several EU countries, Ukraine, North Macedonia, Japan and Brazil, according to the Commission's announcement.

item.title: Separate updates: RAISE launch and Tripartite Social Summit
item.description: Separate official notices: the European Commission launched RAISE in Europe; the Council reported a Tripartite Social Summit meeting in Brussels.

item.title: Agency briefing: aid talks, household finances and science
item.description: Public-agency updates from October 8–9 cover development talks in Dublin, U.S. household finance data and science policy. Read the original sources.
